markers.reading: Departure from Karawa toward Tokra in midmorning.

evidence.quote: DM: Setting off west as the sun rises towards mid morning, nearly three months to the day since you first met in Karawa, you find yourself on the road again. Heading somewhere new. Heading west for new places, new adventures.

time.basis: DM states midmorning; no spoken calendar date.

markers.reading: First travel day ends at the main road in the evening.

evidence.quote: DM: So the first day passes largely uneventfully. You're, you're traveling now, heading, heading sort of northwest basically to connect to the— there's sort of two roads that lead from Karawa: one to the northwest, one to the northeast. The one to the Northeast will eventually fade away into a track that leads to Raven's Hold and then eventually to the mountains and the passes. That's the direction that Drikod has gone. You are heading north west again, along with what's really not, not really even a road. It's just a sort of a beaten track through the desert.

DM: Which will connect with this main, main trade route, the old Drankorian trade route that cuts across the center of Dunmar. And the first you know Day, a day or two you know until you connect to this road probably you'll you'll get to the main road at this evening, but it's it's. You know, leaving Karawa now it's—

DM: Still passing through sort of rolling, rocky desert hills, dry scrub plants, dried up, the— you know, everything sort of baking in the hot sun. You do pass a few Dunmari on their way back from Tokra. You know, everybody is sort of eager to get to Karawa before nightfall and so. You know you just kind of greet people on the road. And on your first night of travel, in the evening of the first night, you do reach this main, main trade route and turn west.

time.basis: Explicit first evening of the journey.

markers.reading: The second travel day reaches camp; the Mirror of the Past has recharged.

evidence.quote: DM: And over the next day, second day of your travel, following the road now you start to, you know, get into the— you know, get a little away from the desert. There's more plants, you— you're, you're gradually descending a tiny bit off the dry high plateaus of the, of the central Dunmar into the—

DM: You know you're not in flowing grasslands, yet you need to go a bit further West or north to get there, but. You can see you can see how this terrain could, you know, support pastoralists and, and herders. And you see, you know, the occasional herd of antelope crossing the, the terrain and, and things like that.
DM: And as you make camp on the second day. The mirror has recharged. If you would like to show something to the mirror.

DM: That was one of the things from Agata's hoard. So the mirror will be recharged tomorrow night. If you have any— I don't wanna, I don't want you to spend the entire session discussing what you're going to use in the mirror. But just as an FYI.
DM: When when it goes dark he he says across the campfire.

time.basis: Second-day camp, with prior prediction of recharge tomorrow night and later campfire conversation.

markers.reading: The coin vision opens on an unidentified road at night; no date is recoverable.

evidence.quote: DM: The scene, the reflection of the, of the campfire and the plains behind you fades, and you see, um, standing in front of you kind of— it's a strange perspective. It almost looks like somebody's flipping the coin up in the air, and so you'll see, like, basically a face, and then it— that the image in the mirror does this tumbling. It's a— it's a—

DM: Sort of a indeterminately aged Chardonian man. You can't see much about his surroundings, he seems to be wearing what you would sort of think of as adventuring gear or sort of almost like, like rogues gear almost, like cloaks, shadows. He, he seems to have a hood over his face, so you can't see that much detail. There is a sense of movement almost like you're traveling on a road. Walking at night. It's dark. Um, just this flipping, flipping, and after about 10, 15 seconds of this, um, on the top of one of the flips, the image shifts.

time.basis: The coin-bearer is walking at night; not the party’s current clock.

markers.reading: The coin vision fades and play returns to the second-day camp.

evidence.quote: DM: Something along those lines, and then the mirror fades.

DM: Yeah so actually that's as you're doing this, he you know once once the mirror has gone dark he he looks up at you, and he says. He's been he's been quiet for most of the trip like just kind of chatting occasionally ah but not, you know, not getting too involved in, in your conversation. Just kind of— it seems like he's been enjoying being on the road, just kind of traveling in the sun, in the wind, kind of remembering what.
Kenzo: You're not being a scarecrow anymore.
DM: Yeah exactly what like wind in hair and sun on flesh feels like.
DM: But when you pull out the mirror he kind of backs away, and when you—
Wellby: When it's gone, oh no this mirror is cool still.
DM: When when it goes dark he he says across the campfire.

markers.reading: Morning of the third travel day; the party crosses into grassland.

evidence.quote: DM: The next morning, um, third day on the road, um. You have now clearly crossed into the, the plains, right? Yeah, you know, as you— every day, it seems to get a little bit more, a little bit more vegetation. Um, you know, the road, road itself, you know a little bit more ah you know, it, it just— it's starting to feel a little bit more like these big open expanses of grassland and kind of more fertile terrain, as you ride in, um.

DM: Ah, there's again still some traffic on the road. Um, hold on one sec. Ah, OK just sent you a message um there's more traffic on the— occasional traffic. And, and here it's not so much like you don't pass people heading to Karawa necessarily. Um, you know, you'll pass, you'll, you'll pass people who are— you see, you know. A few Dunmari hunters following a herd of antelope or you know.

DM: You pass early the morning on the third day on the road, um, um, like family of Dunmari herders with flocks of sheep, sort of not on the road, right? These are people could just live out on these plains, who are you sort of into the— passing into the more settled regions.

time.basis: DM explicitly names morning and the third day.

markers.reading: A quiet travel montage reaches the fifth day at lunchtime. The attempted evening advance is interrupted for aqueduct exploration.

evidence.quote: DM: The next— the next few days pass quietly. You're about halfway there. It's me it's it's been an easy journey.

DM: Again, the road is not crowded, but you never, you know— clearly this is a— people are feeling safe. A lot of people are spreading back out across the plains. You know, especially as you begin to cross over the halfway point and begin to approach Tokra like you know you get a sense of how of like what life in Dunmar was like. You know back a year ago, before all of the devastation and the danger and everything happened, you know.

DM: On the fifth day around lunchtime you pass another small family encampments set off— set up a little bit off the road. Um, there is a— there is a ruined like piece of an aqueduct that runs along the road maybe about a mile north of the road, but clearly visible across the plains, was like a little Dunmari encampments setup there, sheltering in the shade of the, of the aqueduct from the midday sun.
DM: You know that evening of the fifth day you know, you, you pass again— unless you want to go investigate the aqueduct?

time.basis: DM explicitly states fifth day at lunchtime; subsequent evening setup is interrupted.

markers.reading: The party spends a little while investigating the aqueduct.

evidence.quote: DM: So you spend a little while poking around make an investigation check.

markers.reading: Seeker builds an earthen access ramp and collection channel, assisted by camp teenagers, over most of the remaining afternoon.

evidence.quote: Seeker: I set to work on that I can do that making, of course, permanent structures right? With Mold Earth.

DM: Yeah Mold Earth doesn't go away, I mean it just moves around and you're pretty skilled with masonry and architecture. So yeah, it'll take you a, you know, most of the rest of the afternoon, but once they realize what you're doing, you know, several of the like, you know, teenagers running around camp come to help.
Seeker: So I direct the operation, creating a big yeah sort of—
DM: Like an earthen berm that goes up to the.
Seeker: Mm hmm sort of ramp so you can get up.
DM: And—
Seeker: A little channel, so that the water spills out into something that you can gather it and.

time.basis: DM places construction in most of the rest of the afternoon.

duration.text: most of the rest of the afternoon

markers.reading: The party spends the night at the aqueduct camp; the next-morning departure confirms completion.

evidence.quote: DM: So you spend the night.
DM: So the next morning break camp return to the road.

markers.reading: Before that overnight, the grateful hostess serves a meal; this retrospective insertion adds no extra night.

evidence.quote: Kenzo: Wait we eat their food with them right?
DM: Oh yeah yeah so so she's right she's very grateful for all of this um you know what you've done.
Delwath: I'll go poke around and help them cook slash see if I can learn something.

DM: So they so so so she brings out the, like, the nice stuff, right? So they have some, some dried, some dried fruit and, um, just like a nice platter of, like, like flat breads, dried fruit. They've got goat here because they slaughtered a goat a couple days ago, and so they've got goat skewers cooked over the fire, nicely spiced. Some, like like honey cakes for dessert. It's a, it's a pretty good spread. It's, it's like, you know, better. It's all fresh, right? You're mostly eating trail rations, which is pretty much you know, hard goats cheese, hard goat's cheese and, and dried jerky and, like, hard bread or cracker type things, right? So it's nice to get some fresh food, some especially some. You know the the freshly cooked meat and then the honey cake for dessert is a nice treat as well.

DM: So it's a nice meal. Everybody's pleased. Like, the, the kids are like running up the ramp and, like, look— poking around and look at it. Pretty disappointed that, like, anything they pour, nothing happens. Like, try it in the morning, you know.

time.basis: Dinner is inserted immediately after the overnight narration and before next-morning departure.

relations.note: Meal belongs to the same night at camp, before sleep; no additional boundary.

markers.reading: The next morning, the party breaks camp and returns to the road.

evidence.quote: DM: So the next morning break camp return to the road.

time.basis: Explicit next morning after the aqueduct overnight.

markers.reading: Seeker spends a little time looking for ley lines around the aqueduct.

evidence.quote: DM: [garbled] There is actually a ley line that seems to be riding along where this aqueduct is. Well, at the moment there hasn't been one along the road for very long, but as you as you spend a little bit of time looking around right now, it does seem like there's one that, that is, that is following the course of this aqueduct.

markers.reading: Four travel days are narrated; the subsequent correction places the camp on the ninth day on the road, in afternoon/evening.

evidence.quote: DM: The next— the next, you know, three or four days, say the next— the next four days are uneventful as you travel along along this road. Continuing towards Tokra, you're now maybe two days out from Tokra, um, approaching you're still like 50 miles away so you can't like see the River really clearly yet. On clear days it's still like Tokra still a little bit, but beyond the horizon right, so you can't can't quite see it even even given a clear day but with that, like with the days delay to explore the aqueduct at you know your your maybe you'll get there, and about two days from now um. The—

DM: Wow, um, so, you know, it's been about a week. It's been eight— you've been on the road for eight days now, nine days. The mirror having recharged during the course of your travels and looking at the looking at the coin.
DM: And here, as you sort of make camp, the afternoon, evening, a couple days out from Tokra, you have another opportunity to use the mirror if you'd like.
DM: So continuing on do you have any more conversations tonight?

duration.basis: DM corrects three or four to four travel days; this counts travel days rather than asserting four additional midnights.

time.basis: Explicit ninth-day camp after the correction from eight to nine days on the road.

markers.note: From sixth-day morning to ninth-day camp is three calendar transitions, spanning four named travel days.

markers.reading: The next morning after the scorpion camp resumes the journey.

evidence.quote: DM: Okay, so the next morning right you ride again, through the plains. Another uneventful day, uneventful day.

time.basis: Explicit next morning after ninth-day camp.

markers.reading: Early-afternoon approach to Tokra is described as eleven days after leaving Karawa. This may mean the eleventh journey day or eleven elapsed days; retain both ending dates.

evidence.quote: DM: I would say it's probably about early afternoon, 11 days after you left Karawa. You cross the highland and you can see, stretching a few miles beyond, the River Hara winding slowly from north to south, really barely more than a trickle at this time of year before the rains of the monsoon season come. The city of Tokra itself lies just beyond the river, on the other side of a huge arching bridge made of solid greystone that's— that is the only crossing of the Hara for miles in either direction, although realistically you could probably ford it fairly easily. Oh, I guess with your wagon, it— with your cart, it might be trouble, um.

DM: Around the city and this sort of mid afternoon, there's, there's a fair bit of activity. You know, you can see, you know, travelers coming and going on the bridge. There are— what looks like on the far side of the bridge there's you know, a handful of Dunmari soldiers or guards milling about that seemed to be collecting tolls from from everybody who passes.

DM: And you know there's some activity in the army camp in the distance of— seems to be, can see the plumes of dust rising up from horses riding, doing drills or patrols or something like that, and just the general bustle of activity. You can hear, you know, echoing from the distance, the clang of metal on metal of somebody you know hammering horseshoes or the the general bustle of city life rises up from the River Valley.
DM: You are now— so you're coming on the crest of the hill. You're going to descend now on a gentle slope to the bridge, maybe a mile from where you are now. So just go across the bridge?

time.basis: Explicit DM anchor; relative day count remains ambiguous.

markers.note: Conditional on June 20 departure, inclusive day eleven is June 30; eleven elapsed days is July 1.

markers.reading: Arrival at the Lakan Monastery around sunset on the Tokra approach day.

evidence.quote: DM: And you turn and ride up the road to the monastery arriving around sunset.
